domain.name: Entrepreneurship & Market Research
domain.description: Practical customer discovery, market sizing, competition, business models, validation, go-to-market, strategic advantage, and opportunity prioritization.

competencies.name: Customer Discovery
competencies.description: Learn real customer problems, constraints, alternatives, and buying behavior.
competencies.purpose: Learn real customer problems, constraints, alternatives, and buying behavior.

units.title: Customer Discovery: core principle
units.content: Recent behavior and real commitments are stronger evidence than hypothetical enthusiasm.

units.title: Customer Discovery: working procedure
units.content: Define learning goal; ask about recent behavior, current workaround, cost/friction, decision process, and failed alternatives; delay pitching until learning is complete.

units.title: Customer Discovery: common failures
units.content: Avoid leading questions, interviewing only friends, pitching during research, and counting compliments as demand.

drills.title: Practice Customer Discovery
drills.prompt: Create a discovery guide for local businesses considering short-form ad production.

competencies.name: Market Sizing
competencies.description: Estimate realistic opportunity from customers, spend, frequency, geography, and reachable segments.
competencies.purpose: Estimate realistic opportunity from customers, spend, frequency, geography, and reachable segments.

units.title: Market Sizing: core principle
units.content: A smaller reachable market can be more valuable than a giant theoretical market with no credible route to customers.

units.title: Market Sizing: working procedure
units.content: Define target customer; estimate reachable count; annual spend/frequency; broad potential; narrow to reachable share and service capacity; document assumptions.

units.title: Market Sizing: common failures
units.content: Avoid using global industry revenue as local opportunity, assuming every prospect buys, and ignoring capacity.

drills.title: Practice Market Sizing
drills.prompt: Estimate a reachable market for event photo/video using segments, event counts, average spend, and capacity.

competencies.name: Competitive Analysis
competencies.description: Understand alternatives, positioning, price signals, strengths, and gaps.
competencies.purpose: Understand alternatives, positioning, price signals, strengths, and gaps.

units.title: Competitive Analysis: core principle
units.content: The real competitor may be DIY, delay, internal staff, or doing nothing.

units.title: Competitive Analysis: working procedure
units.content: Map direct and substitute alternatives; audience; offer; price cues; proof; channels; strengths; weaknesses; validate gaps with customer evidence.

units.title: Competitive Analysis: common failures
units.content: Avoid judging only websites, assuming list price equals realized price, and copying competitors without strategic reason.

drills.title: Practice Competitive Analysis
drills.prompt: Map agencies, freelancers, DIY tools, and in-house alternatives for 60-second ads.

competencies.name: Business Model Design
competencies.description: Connect customer value, revenue, delivery, costs, channels, and key resources.
competencies.purpose: Connect customer value, revenue, delivery, costs, channels, and key resources.

units.title: Business Model Design: core principle
units.content: Revenue model and delivery model must fit each other; recurring billing requires recurring value and workable recurring delivery.

units.title: Business Model Design: working procedure
units.content: Define customer, problem, value proposition, offer, acquisition, revenue, delivery process, variable/fixed costs, resources, risks, and retention mechanics.

units.title: Business Model Design: common failures
units.content: Avoid projecting revenue without acquisition cost, ignoring capacity, and assuming high margins before measuring real delivery effort.

drills.title: Practice Business Model Design
drills.prompt: Map a short-form ad service business model including acquisition, pricing, delivery, revisions, capacity, and recurring options.

competencies.name: Offer Validation
competencies.description: Test whether a specific offer produces meaningful commitment before scaling.
competencies.purpose: Test whether a specific offer produces meaningful commitment before scaling.

units.title: Offer Validation: core principle
units.content: Time, money, access, data, or a scheduled next step are stronger than likes and compliments.

units.title: Offer Validation: working procedure
units.content: Define audience/outcome; create concrete offer and price; test with qualified prospects; ask for meaningful commitment; track objections; revise based on evidence.

units.title: Offer Validation: common failures
units.content: Avoid changing audience and offer simultaneously, free trials that attract non-buyers, and scaling fulfillment before understanding why people buy.

drills.title: Practice Offer Validation
drills.prompt: Design a two-week validation plan for a monthly content package.

competencies.name: Go-to-Market Strategy
competencies.description: Choose channels, messaging, sales motion, launch sequence, and feedback loops.
competencies.purpose: Choose channels, messaging, sales motion, launch sequence, and feedback loops.

units.title: Go-to-Market Strategy: core principle
units.content: Channel fit depends on where qualified buyers can be reached credibly, not where the biggest audience exists.

units.title: Go-to-Market Strategy: working procedure
units.content: Define ICP, trigger/problem, positioning, primary acquisition channel, message, proof, sales/checkout motion, onboarding, metrics, and feedback cadence.

units.title: Go-to-Market Strategy: common failures
units.content: Avoid launching on every channel at once, no follow-up path, inconsistent positioning, and measuring reach without qualified pipeline.

drills.title: Practice Go-to-Market Strategy
drills.prompt: Build a go-to-market plan for DFB commercial video services targeting local businesses.

competencies.name: Strategic Advantage & Moats
competencies.description: Build durable advantages from brand, data, workflow, distribution, IP, switching costs, or economics.
competencies.purpose: Build durable advantages from brand, data, workflow, distribution, IP, switching costs, or economics.

units.title: Strategic Advantage & Moats: core principle
units.content: A meaningful moat becomes stronger through repeated use, customers, reputation, data, or distribution.

units.title: Strategic Advantage & Moats: working procedure
units.content: Inventory assets/capabilities; test uniqueness and durability; identify compounding loops; choose investments that strengthen those loops.

units.title: Strategic Advantage & Moats: common failures
units.content: Avoid calling ordinary features proprietary, confusing complexity with defensibility, and assuming first-mover status persists.

drills.title: Practice Strategic Advantage & Moats
drills.prompt: Evaluate DFB workflows, client history, local reputation, owned content systems, and IP for durable advantage potential.

competencies.name: Opportunity Prioritization
competencies.description: Compare opportunities using cash potential, leverage, fit, effort, risk, and distraction.
competencies.purpose: Compare opportunities using cash potential, leverage, fit, effort, risk, and distraction.

units.title: Opportunity Prioritization: core principle
units.content: Opportunity cost is real: a decent idea can still be the wrong use of limited attention.

units.title: Opportunity Prioritization: working procedure
units.content: Estimate near-term cash, margin, repeatability, owned leverage, fit, startup effort, complexity, capital need, downside, and opportunity cost; decide advance/hold/kill.

units.title: Opportunity Prioritization: common failures
units.content: Avoid optimistic scoring, ignoring founder attention, sunk-cost thinking, and pursuing ideas with no next evidence milestone.

drills.title: Practice Opportunity Prioritization
drills.prompt: Rank a local service, software product, and content channel using cash, leverage, fit, risk, and effort.
